name: Install DevStack
description:
we covered these steps on OpenStack basics under topic Install and Configure DevStack. And couple of time during Cinder and Glance. This time, we will run a wrapper script which will download the repo and setup config files. Just run the wrapper script after updating the system 
sudo apt-get update  
sudo apt-get -y install git

wget -O- http://giis.co.in/install_devstack.sh | bash

Okay done, please check the local.conf and openrc files. Lets run the devstack script, you know it will around ~30 minutes.

sudo su stack
cd ~
 /home/stack/openstack/stack.sh

name: OpenStack Commandline
description:
So far, we have used Horizon dashboard to create instance, but real admins use command-line :) Cinder is an OpenStack project to provide block storage as a service. On this lesson we will use commandline to practise and learn about following Cinder tasks:

  • Creating a volume
  • Attach volume to an instance
  • Detach volume from an instance
  • Resize a volume
  • Delete a volume

We have exported env variable like OS_AUTH_URL,OS_USERNAME,OS_PASSWORD, OS_TENANT_NAME,OS_PROJECT_NAME on /home/stack/openstack/openrc file we need to import them into our current shell like

source /home/stack/openstack/openrc

name: Create and attach a volume
description:
create a new volume wmvol with 1GB size
cinder create 1 --display-name wmvol

type
cinder list
to view its status. Its in available state. cinder list 
                           
+--------------------------------------+-----------+-------+------+-----
|ID        |   Status |Name | Size| Volume Type| Bootable | Attached to|                                             
+--------------------------------------+-----------+-------+------+-----
| 2169614f-| available|wmvol|  1  | lvmdriver-1|  false   |            |                                                      
+--------------------------------------+-----------+-------+------+-----

Create keypair:
nova keypair-add wmkey > wmkey.pem

chmod 600 wmkey.pem
and launch an instance:
nova boot --flavor m1.tiny --image cirros-0.3.4-x86_64-uec --key-name wmkey wmvm
List volumes, notice status of volume and note its ID.
cinder list
Now we will attached the volume using its ID to our instance(wmvm) as /dev/vdb
nova volume-attach wmvm 2169614f-19d3-4220-904a-055a8fa3258c
When you run above command, you can see details like, where its mounted along with server and volume ID.

Now using cinder list command, you can verify status 'in-use' and 'Attached to' outputs.
+--------------------------------------+--------+-------+------+-------------+
|ID         | Status |  Name | Size | Volume Type | Bootable |  Attached to  
+--------------------------------------+--------+-------+------+-------------+
| 2169614f- | in-use | wmvol |  1   | lvmdriver-1 |  false   | 40f870d3- |   
+--------------------------------------+--------+-------+------+----------

We just launched an instance, can we verifying this with Horizon Dashboard?.
answer:
Answer is 'Yes', afterall, whenever we use Horizon dashboard, they invoke these commands internally. So login to dashboard with admin/password and see for yourself. Needless to say, Dashboard URL:

 http://HOST_IP

In fact, whatever you do on commandline should reflect on Horizon dashboard. If it didn't, congrats you found a bug in OpenStack Horizon :) Please file a bug on OpenStack or write to us we will file it on your behalf!

name: Format the volume
description:
In order to ssh into instance, we need to find out the ipaddress:
nova list 
                                                                                                           
+--------------------------------------+------+--------+------------+------                                                        
| ID        | Name | Status |TaskState| Power State | Networks         |                                                        
+--------------------------------------+------+--------+------------+------                                                        
| 40f870d3- | wmvm | ACTIVE |  | Running     | private=10.0.0.2 |                                                        
+--------------------------------------+------+--------+------------+------

Can you see the ipaddress? Just use it like,
ssh -i wmkey.pem cirros@10.0.0.2
We need to list devices via
sudo fdisk -l

Should produce output like 
    ...
    ...
Disk /dev/vdb: 1073 MB, 1073741824 bytes                             
16 heads, 63 sectors/track, 2080 cylinders, total 2097152 sectors   
Units = sectors of 1 * 512 = 512 bytes                               
Sector size (logical/physical): 512 bytes / 512 bytes               
I/O size (minimum/optimal): 512 bytes / 512 bytes                   
Disk identifier: 0x00000000                                         
Disk /dev/vdb doesn't contain a valid partition table
0. On the instance, make file system on volume.
sudo mkfs.ext3 /dev/vdb
1. Create a mountpoint
sudo mkdir /newdisk
2. Mount the volume at the mountpoint
sudo mount /dev/vdb /newdisk && df -h 
Filesystem                Size      Used Available Use% MountedOn  
...                                            
/dev/vdb               1007.9M     33.3M    923.4M   3% /newdisk

3. Create a file on the volume
sudo touch /newdisk/file.txt

sudo ls /newdisk
4. Finally, unmount the volume
sudo umount /newdisk

name: Exercise for you!
description:
Lets test your nova and cinder command-line skills!

Do you think, you can perform below tasks without looking at the answer? :)

Here's some task for you. Now we have file.txt on wmvol.
1.Launch a new instance named 'wmvm2' with nova boot command.

2.Detach wmvol from older instance wmvm using nova volume-detach command.

3.Attach the volume wmvol to newly launched wmvm2 and access file.txt within that instance.
answer:
1. nova boot --flavor m1.tiny --image cirros-0.3.4-x86_64-uec --key-name wmkey wmvm2
2.nova volume-detach wmvm 2169614f-19d3-4220-904a-055a8fa3258c
3.nova volume-attach wmvm2 2169614f-19d3-4220-904a-055a8fa3258c
Perform fdisk and mount it. Beware,don't format the drive

name: Resize and Delete a Volume
description:
Lets say, we want to increase the volume size from 1GB to 2GB. We can perform such task with extend command.

cinder extend wmvol 2

Finally, lets cleanup our resource and delete it

cinder delete wmvol

For credits and source: http://docs.openstack.org/
